A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same simulator, renamed from GauSim to GausSim. All 16 pages of v1 and 15 pages of v2, including their five-page supplements, support comparison. Equations, figures and experiments can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original READY dataset experiments, comparisons with PhysDreamer, physics-constraint ablations, joint-training results and interactive simulations.

after.justification: v2 reports original real and synthetic dynamics experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations, timing and memory measurements, and foreground-color analysis.

M1.justification: The backbone, deformation updates, CMS hierarchy, physics constraints and training losses are retained. Emphasizing individual kernels as CMSs restates v1 Section 3.3 and Appendix A2.2. The interactive-force procedure moves to Appendix A4.4 without changing.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands from three real READY objects to four by adding Carnation, and introduces synthetic Bunny dynamics generated using Blender. Bunny's reduced damping adds sustained-motion conditions, substantially broadening coverage beyond the original real-object collection.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates only PhysDreamer against GauSim. v2 retains it as PD and adds DreamGaussian4D, or DG4D, throughout the quantitative and qualitative comparisons, broadening comparison to a reconstruction-based approach. PhysGaussian still has no separate result entries.

E3.justification: Table 1 replaces the original Unseen 17/34 reporting with Unseen 83 for Mothorchids, Pudding and Carnation, and Unseen 34 for Duck and Bunny. Seen frames are stated as t=0–15 instead of t=0–16. New protocols include looping DG4D's training reconstructions and measuring efficiency over 50 prediction frames on one A100. The stated Unseen 83 interval, t=16–99, retains a frame-count ambiguity.

E4.justification: Table 2 adds a hierarchy-removal ablation measuring runtime and memory, directly testing a central component's resource benefits. Appendix Table A3 adds foreground-color and error-scale analysis. These introduce substantive analytical questions alongside the retained mass/momentum and joint-training ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions report sequence-averaged errors with ± quantities without defining their statistical meaning or documenting repeated training runs and seeds. v2 uses the same reporting style for timing. No new confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated-run scheme are specified.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds dataset and comparator results and revises existing scores beyond an equivalent rescaling. Under the revised windows, Table 3 changes from the momentum-free variant having the lowest errors to the full model having the lowest. Table 2 adds measured efficiency: 0.13 seconds and 2.1 GB with hierarchy versus 0.36 seconds and 3.5 GB without, while dropping Pudding/Duck kernel-count entries. Changed windows and newly stated 10^-3 units prevent interpreting cross-version scores as direct performance gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical assumptions, continuum formulations, conservation derivations and Appendix A2 proofs are retained. v1 Equations 6–8 are regrouped into v2 Equations 6–7; the remaining differences are renumbering, heading changes and relocation of the interactive equations.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the continuum-based simulator, CMS hierarchy, physics constraints and READY dataset. The quantitative efficiency claim changes from around 90% fewer predictions to around 95% in the introduction and Section 3.3, with v2 Table 2 demonstrating the latter specifically on Mothorchids.

C2.justification: v2 extends v1's warning about low errors from static predictions with explanations involving foreground contrast, reduced Bunny damping and the need for qualitative evaluation. It adds interpretations of joint training's faster dissipation and PD's difficulties with stiff, rapidly oscillating objects. The stated data-quality and reconstruction limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A4.2 newly documents baseline tuning, including PD's Young's modulus search from 1 to 5×10^8 and grid-size variation. Table A2 adds clustering radii for Carnation and Bunny. Existing backbone and training details are largely relocated unchanged; the code/model release promise and project address remain.

R1.justification: The unique cited works and related-work survey remain effectively unchanged; duplicate spring-mass Gaussian references are consolidated. A limited positioning refinement argues that PD can represent PhysGaussian through their shared MPM framework and explicitly contrasts DG4D's reconstruction capability with forecasting.

P1.justification: The title and method name change, CMS terminology is clarified, and experimental interpretation is rewritten. Implementation and interactive-application passages move into the supplement. The overall section sequence and most methodological, related-work and proof prose retain their structure.

P2.justification: The experimental displays are substantially redesigned: Table 1 gains dataset columns and a comparator row, Table 2 becomes a combined count/resource display, and Table 3 is transposed. The qualitative and space-time figures are reordered and expanded, Figure A1 is rebuilt, Figure 5 is shortened, and Table A3 is added.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for central claims. v1 supported efficiency mainly through prediction counts; v2 adds measured runtime and memory with a hierarchy-removal control. The reduced-damping Bunny evaluation tests sustained motion, while the color analysis makes pixel-error limitations more explicit. Losing separate early-unseen scores reduces diagnostic detail, and looped DG4D remains a limited forecasting reference, but the new direct efficiency evidence and broader motion validation provide a substantial net quality gain.
